clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive chromosomal-instability disorder caused by biallelic variants in NBN, encoding nibrin, a component of the MRE11-RAD50-NBN complex involved in DNA double-strand break repair
Progressive microcephaly is present from birth or infancy and is a cardinal feature, accompanied by a characteristic bird-like facial appearance
Combined immunodeficiency causes recurrent respiratory and other infections, with low immunoglobulins and reduced lymphocyte subsets
There is a very high risk of malignancy in childhood, predominantly lymphomas and leukaemias, but also solid tumours
Growth restriction and, in females, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism with ovarian failure are common
Cells show increased chromosomal breakage and characteristic rearrangements involving chromosomes 7 and 14, with radiosensitivity
There is a founder variant common in Slavic populations, and marked radiosensitivity means ionising radiation should be avoided wherever possible
reference.pathophysiology: Nijmegen breakage syndrome is caused by biallelic hypomorphic variants in NBN, encoding nibrin, a subunit of the MRE11-RAD50-NBN (MRN) complex that senses and initiates repair of DNA double-strand breaks and coordinates cell-cycle checkpoint signalling through the ATM pathway. Impaired nibrin function leaves cells unable to repair double-strand breaks efficiently, producing chromosomal instability, characteristic rearrangements and hypersensitivity to ionising radiation. This defect underlies the immunodeficiency (from impaired lymphocyte development requiring efficient DNA recombination), the microcephaly and the strong predisposition to lymphoid and other malignancies.
additionalDifferentials: LIG4 syndrome and other DNA double-strand break repair defects
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing of NBN to confirm biallelic variants
Cytogenetic analysis showing chromosomal instability and rearrangements involving chromosomes 7 and 14
Immunological workup including immunoglobulin levels and lymphocyte subsets
Serial neuroimaging and growth monitoring for microcephaly and growth restriction
Symptom-directed cancer surveillance, favouring non-ionising imaging
redFlags: New lymphadenopathy, organomegaly or cytopenias suggesting lymphoma or leukaemia
Severe or recurrent infections indicating significant immunodeficiency
Unexpected severe toxicity after exposure to ionising radiation
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is poor, driven principally by the very high childhood risk of lymphoid and other cancers and by complications of immunodeficiency. Radiosensitivity constrains both diagnostic imaging and cancer treatment, and management is largely supportive with infection prophylaxis and vigilant, radiation-sparing cancer monitoring.
pitfalls: Exposing patients to avoidable ionising radiation for imaging or radiotherapy given their radiosensitivity
Ascribing microcephaly to a non-genetic cause and missing the diagnosis
Underestimating the degree of immunodeficiency and infection risk
Delaying investigation of possible lymphoma because symptoms overlap with infection
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Manage the immunodeficiency with immunoglobulin replacement and antimicrobial prophylaxis, and treat infections promptly
Minimise ionising radiation because of profound radiosensitivity: avoid diagnostic X-rays and CT and favour non-ionising ultrasound and MRI
Undertake symptom-directed cancer surveillance focused on lymphoma and leukaemia, using non-ionising imaging
Modify oncological treatment when malignancy occurs, reducing radiotherapy and radiomimetic chemotherapy doses because of radiosensitivity
Provide hormone replacement for hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and ovarian failure in affected females
Monitor growth and neurodevelopment and provide developmental support for microcephaly and growth restriction
Consider haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in selected patients
Coordinate multidisciplinary care and offer genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance
